claims: Centrus sits at a domestic enrichment/HALEU bottleneck connecting uranium feed and enrichment technology to advanced-reactor fuel availability, energy security and national-security needs.

DOE-supported scale-up and binding customer additions support demand visibility, but durable bottleneck control depends on converting demonstration capability into reliable commercial-scale enrichment.
causalEdges: uranium feed -> enrichment capacity -> HALEU -> advanced reactors/microreactors -> reliable low-carbon and defense energy needs
DOE/customer funding -> cascade expansion -> commercial supply capacity
commercial delivery performance -> customer confidence -> backlog conversion
substitutes: foreign enrichment supply where policy permits
alternative reactor designs using LEU/LEU+ rather than HALEU
counterfactuals: If advanced-reactor deployment slips or designs migrate away from HALEU, the strategic enrichment bottleneck remains relevant but company-specific demand conversion slows.
falsifiers: failure to scale enrichment capacity despite funding
material customer cancellations or reactor schedule slippage
credible domestic substitute capacity eroding scarcity

claims: Recent customer contracts and DOE support evidence demand but do not prove delivered commercial-scale volumes or margins.

The September 2026 equity/warrant financing increases funding capacity while creating dilution/overhang; federal-policy and procurement dependence remain structural exposures rather than automatic blockers.
improvementPaths: report contracted deliveries converting to recognized commercial output
falsifiers: repeatable commercial deliveries at attractive margins with diversified customers would materially weaken execution and concentration challenges
